headline: Every pouch checked, all 290 million a year.
label: #FFFFFF
heroLede: With that many flavours through Wodonga, the label is what tells one pouch from the next. Here's what a camera check could look like on your pouch lines. Scroll through, then adjust the estimate at the end to your own numbers.
lidLede: The camera checks every pouch is sealed straight across, with no crease and no food caught in the seal. A weak seal on a retorted pouch is a spoiled pouch in someone’s pantry.
labelLede: Chicken in gravy and tuna in jelly pouches look much the same at line speed. The camera checks every pouch carries the right label for the flavour inside, straight and intact, so the pet owner gets what the pack says.
codeLede: The best-before and batch code has to be right and readable on every pouch. The system reads the printed code and compares it with the flavour and date set at changeover.
objectLede: Film offcuts, glove pieces and loose parts can end up on the conveyor. The camera over the belt spots anything that should not be there before it reaches a case.

vocab.alert: Four creased seals in fifteen minutes on Line 1. Check the pouch sealer.

extra: 38% of Australian food recalls in 2025 were for undeclared allergens, with packaging errors among the main causes. FSANZ
With hundreds of millions of pouches a year, even one wrong label in ten thousand is tens of thousands of pouches. That is our example figure, not yours.
